title.narrative: Feasibility study Kilimanjaro Blind Trust Africa

description.narrative: It is difficult for people who are blind or visually impaired to use smartphones, laptops and computers. Hable One B.V., a startup from Eindhoven, has designed a compact external remote control and keyboard, 'the Hable One', that makes using and controlling these devices easier and more convenient for people with a visual impairment. With the Hable One, the user can do everything on the smartphone etc, from typing text and messages to controlling the entire phone or tablet. Their access to information, communication and quality education is thereby considerably increased, which ensures more autonomy and integration – social and economic – in society.The Kilimanjaro Blind Trust Afria (KBTA), an NGO based in Nairobi, focuses on using innovative assistive (Braille) technologies to ensure that children and young adults with visual impairments can learn in schools, colleges, universities and other institutions. KBTA has already purchased several thousand Orbit Readers, a portable braille display, for students in the past. The Orbit Reader is three times as expensive as the Hable One. KBTA has now expressed interest in purchasing 2,000 Hable One devices for young people with a visual impairment to help them participate in education and the labour market. But first, KBTA wants a number of technical, functional and financial aspects to be worked out before a final investment decision is taken.A small pilot with a number of students and teachers from two Kenyan universities will be part of the project.
